$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.grammar.haxe. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-ALWAYS-NEXT
arms.note: every value of sameLine.comprehensionFor becomes `next`, so a body the key asked to keep on the head line leaves it

arms.name: M-ARROW-BODY-PAD-KEY-OFF
arms.note: objectLiteralBraces.arrowBodyOpenPad:true is read as false, so an arrow-lambda-body literal loses its open pad again under a config that asked to keep it

arms.name: M-ARROW-BODY-PAD-KEY-IGNORED
arms.note: objectLiteralBraces.arrowBodyOpenPad:false is read as true, so a caller who asked for the open pad dropped after `->` still gets it

arms.name: M-ARROW-BODY-PAD-DEFAULT-OFF
arms.note: an arrow-lambda-body object literal drops its open pad again under the default options, so the braces pad `{a: 1 }`

arms.name: M-ALWAYS-SAME
arms.note: every value of sameLine.comprehensionFor becomes `same`, so `keep` stops reproducing the source break

arms.name: M-FANOUT-FIRST
replace:
if (section.comprehensionFor != null) opt.expressionForBody = HaxeFormatValues.bodyPolicyToRuntime(section.comprehensionFor, opt.expressionForBody);
	applyExpressionIfFanout(section, opt);
arms.note: the specific comprehensionFor key is read BEFORE the general expressionIf fanout, so the fanout clobbers it — the S77 precedence PERMUTED, which is what its note asked for and what one find/replace pair could not express

arms.name: M-KINDS
arms.note: CONTAINER_PLAIN collapses into NONE, so the generated forwarder and the classifier stop agreeing on the four codes

arms.name: M-NO-WIRE
arms.note: the one read that wires sameLine.comprehensionFor is gone, so the key goes back to the inert state S77 found it in

arms.name: M-EXPR-ELSE-NEXT
arms.note: `sameLine.expressionIf: next` maps the else-gap to `Next`, so a value-`if` with a `{ … }` branch puts its `else` on the line after the `}` while its statement twin joins

arms.name: M-EXPR-ELSE-PLAIN-SAME
arms.note: the refuted cheap fix, wired as an arm: `next` maps onto a plain `Same`, so the shape-aware bracket arm joins an `else` onto a `]` and the curly `;` drop stops firing

arms.name: M-ELSE-BODY-SAME
arms.note: the else BODY stops following `expressionIf: next`, so the shape-aware forced break is suppressed and `SameOnBlock` joins an `else` onto an object-literal close

arms.name: M-OPAQUE-REGION-HAND-LIST
arms.note: the fallback-ctor family is enumerated by hand again, exactly as it stood on 2026-08-18 instead of being derived from the grammar's `@:condRegionRaw` terminals - the three raw-capture ctors the grammar gained two days later (both `return` splices and the metadata-prefixed `MetaCondStmt`) fall out of the gate and every name-driven op rewrites around such a region in silence

arms.name: M-COND-BLOCK-TAIL-NEVER
arms.note: the block-tail terminal never matches, so a `#if` region that closes its enclosing block and opens one of its own falls back to CondSpliceStmt and the whole region is raw bytes again

arms.name: M-PATTERN-RESTPROBE-UNSET
arms.note: the pattern subtree never declines the rest-of-line fit bias, so a ctor below a collection pattern is charged the trailing guard and breaks its own args

arms.name: M-DECL-HOST-KIND-STALE
arms.note: a retired ctor name is put back into a kind set the hand-written side declares - the exact shape of this slice's real catch, where `LambdaParam` outlived the grammar rule that projected it by three months. A dead name in a kind set changes no behaviour, so no other test can see it and only the subset assertion goes red

arms.name: M-ELLIPSIS-STMT-TOKEN-STALE
arms.note: the statement-scope `....` placeholder is respelled as a five-dot token. The ctor stays declared and stays projected, and no source under PARSE_ROOTS spells the token at all, so nothing in the tree changes except that one row of the kind-source table stops emitting the kind it claims - the fail-open shape the coverage census exists to see

arms.name: M-AND-OPERATOR-TEXT-STALE
arms.note: the declared logical-and token is respelled as the bitwise one, which still parses and still is an operator, so nothing in the tree breaks and the shape simply names text the parser reads as a different node

arms.name: M-CONSTRUCTOR-NAME-PADDED
arms.note: the declared constructor name gains a trailing space, so the probe source is `function new () {}` - it still parses, the FnMember still SPANS text holding `new `, and only the projected NAME stops being the declared token. The span-containment reading this arm was written against is green on it; the name-slot reading is what goes red

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-CHAIN-EMPTY
arms.note: the grammar reports no ambient source for any module and calls the empty chain bounded, so every name an `import.hx` binds is invisible again while nothing refuses to pin

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-CHAIN-ROOT
arms.note: no module has a computable source root, so the chain shrinks to the module's own directory and every ancestor ambient source is lost

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-GOVERNANCE-BLIND
arms.note: no file is recognised as an ambient import source, so its statements are judged against its own text — which is nothing but those statements — and every one of them reads as dead

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-GOVERNANCE-SHORT
arms.note: the modules an ambient source governs are never reported as fully enumerated, so every verdict about such a file is withheld and a dead statement in one is never found

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-GOVERNANCE-COMPLETE
arms.note: a governed set that could not be listed is claimed complete, so an ambient source whose readers the engine never saw has every statement called dead and deleted

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-IMPORT-MAP
arms.note: the import map drops the path it was given, so every type-aware reader of it sees a module's own imports and never what its ambient chain binds

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-DISK-BLIND
arms.note: the chain is walked for a module that is not on disk, so an analysed source with an invented path takes the ambient bindings of whatever directory its path happens to name

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-UNREADABLE-BOUNDED
arms.note: an ambient source that exists and could not be read is reported as a complete chain, so a consumer pins a reference against bindings the engine never saw

arms.name: M-REACH-STRINGBUF-PURE
arms.note: a string buffer write counts as code that may change the caller's array

arms.name: M-ENTRY-POINT-UNREACHED
arms.note: `static function main()` is an ordinary private method, so `unused-private` deletes the program's entry point

arms.name: M-ENTRY-POINT-ANY-ARITY
arms.note: a `main` taking parameters counts as the entry point, which the compiler never calls

arms.name: M-FOLD-CONSTANT-AS-EXPRESSION
arms.note: a constant operand or block decomposes as an expression again, so the fold writes '${0} ' for 0 + ' ' and the re-render keeps the block

arms.name: M-CONSTANT-NEGATIVE-ZERO-SIGNED
arms.note: a negated zero is spliced as -0, while the Int it evaluates to prints 0

arms.name: M-CONSTANT-FLOAT-ADMITTED
arms.note: a Float literal counts as target-invariant text, though 1.0 prints 1 on js and 1.0 on python

arms.name: M-CONSTANT-HEX-RANGE-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a hex literal past 0x7FFFFFFF is spliced as its unsigned value, though the Int it types as wraps negative

arms.name: M-CONSTANT-DECIMAL-RANGE-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a decimal literal past 2147483647 counts as Int text, though it types as Float and prints per target

arms.name: M-SHAPE-PURE-GETENV
arms.note: (precision) an environment read may run project code

arms.name: M-TS-BUILTIN-EVENTS
arms.note: a datagram read, a result set's length and the event loop's waits block only where a project lists them

arms.name: M-SEARCH-TRY-EXPR-UNRELATED
arms.note: a `try` pattern parses through the Stmt attempt and no longer matches a `try` used as a value (an initializer, an argument, a return value), nor a braced value body - the shape a parse-or-null sweep exists to find, reported as 0 hits

arms.name: M-VOCAB-DOWHILE-EXPR-NOT-LOOP
arms.note: a do-while in expression position (`() -> do x while (c)`) is no loop to any reader of the loop vocabulary

arms.name: M-NAMED-FN-STMT-NO-ARM
arms.note: `x = function n() { return 1; } trace(x());` no longer parses: the named literal's `}` does not end the statement

arms.name: M-NAMED-FN-NOT-BRACE-ENDED
arms.note: `var g = function n() { … }` keeps a `;` the anonymous spelling drops: the var-rhs gate reads the named literal as not brace-ended

arms.name: M-NAMED-FN-EXPR-BODY-RELAXED
arms.note: a named literal's EXPRESSION body ends its statement with no `;`, so `x = function n() return 1 trace(x());` (Haxe: `Missing ;`) parses

arms.name: M-VOCAB-WHILE-EXPR-NOT-BRANCH
arms.note: a `while` comprehension or lambda body is no decision point: complexity counts nothing for it and a binding under it is hoisted

arms.name: M-RESERVED-IDENT-NAME
arms.note: a declaration name (parameter, binder, type, enum constructor, structure field) takes a reserved word Haxe refuses

arms.name: M-RESERVED-VAR-NAME
arms.note: a `var` / `final` name takes every reserved word but `var` and `final` again

arms.name: M-RESERVED-FN-NAME
arms.note: a function name takes a reserved word Haxe refuses

arms.name: M-RESERVED-VERSIONED-REFUSED
arms.note: a `var` name refuses `operator` / `overload` too, and a module declaring one under a `#if` for an older Haxe skip-parses

arms.name: M-NARROWING-OR-FLAT
arms.note: every `||` a boolean reduction writes joins flat, stranding a null test past the first operand

arms.name: M-NARROWING-OR-COMPOUND-ADMITTED
arms.note: a null comparison buried in a compound operand no longer refuses a reduction whose later operand it narrows

arms.name: M-NARROWING-OR-GLUE-COMMENT-ADMITTED
arms.note: a regrouped chain drops a comment standing between two of its operands

arms.name: M-NARROWING-OR-INNER-COMMENT-ADMITTED
arms.note: a regrouped chain joins an operand whose span carries a line comment, which swallows the rest of the line

arms.name: M-OR-LEAVES-OR-OPAQUE
arms.note: an `||` is one opaque operand, so a null test inside it is never seen as stranded

arms.name: M-OR-LEAVES-NEGATED-AND-OPAQUE
arms.note: a negated `&&` is one opaque operand, so the De Morgan `||` it writes is never regrouped

arms.name: M-TERNARY-OR-BRANCH-UNREAD
arms.find: orLeaves(elseNode, false, source, typeNominalOf, orLeaves(cond, false, source, typeNominalOf, []))
arms.note: the kept branch is left out of the `||` chain the reduction judges, so a null test inside it is never regrouped

arms.name: M-GUARD-CHAIN-NEGATED-RUN-DROPPED
arms.note: a negated `&&` guard's `||` is one opaque operand of the chain before it, so its null test strands

arms.name: M-NAMING-ENUMVALUE-PROPERTY
arms.note: a property of an enum abstract (`var x(get, never)`) reads as one of its values again

arms.name: M-NAMING-ENUMVALUE-STATIC
arms.note: a static member of an enum abstract reads as one of its values again

arms.name: M-NAMING-ALLOWGRANT-AS-ANNOTATION
arms.note: a member carrying only @:allow is refused as annotated again

arms.name: M-XREN-EXTENDS-KIND-DROPPED
arms.note: the `ExtendsField` node is no type reference again, so `uses` and `rename --scope` are blind to a typedef's `> T`

arms.name: M-SORTED-RAW-ESCAPES
arms.note: an escaped or interpolated literal sorts by its RAW text, which is not its value

arms.name: M-NAMING-PROPERTY-MODS-NONE
arms.note: no property earns a storage modifier, so a storage-less private property needs the `_` again and a static read-only one is a camelCase public field

arms.name: M-NAMING-STORAGELESS-ISVAR
arms.note: an `@:isVar` property counts as storage-less, so its storage escapes the private-field rule

arms.name: M-NAMING-STORAGELESS-REGION
arms.note: a run that steps over a `#if` region counts as proven, so an `@:isVar` one build sees there is missed

arms.name: M-NAMING-STORAGELESS-RULE-PUBLIC
arms.note: the storage-less property rule reaches a PUBLIC property, whose `_` the public-field rule rejects

arms.name: M-NAMING-READONLY-RULE-INSTANCE
arms.note: an INSTANCE read-only property takes the static-final format too

arms.name: M-SHAPE-COMMUTATIVE-UNSET
arms.note: the grammar names no commutativity annotation, so no overload is tried swapped and a misfit leaves the walk undecided

arms.name: M-COND-PARAM-ELSE-PLAIN
arms.note: the `#else` arm of a parameter region captures no per-element separator, so the comma it writes before `#end` is lost and that arm compiles two parameters with nothing between them

arms.name: M-COND-PARAM-ELSEIF-PLAIN
arms.note: an `#elseif` arm of a parameter region captures no per-element separator, so the comma it writes before the next directive is lost

arms.name: M-ENUM-CTOR-PARAMS-PLAIN
arms.note: an enum constructor's parameters capture no per-element separator, so every gap gets a comma and a region already ending on its own is followed by `#end, c:Int`

arms.name: M-TERNARY-MLB-NO-DESCENT
arms.note: a block below the branch top (a function argument, an object-literal value) is not found, so `inline` breaks those ternaries

arms.name: M-TERNARY-MLB-PATH-UNSEARCHED
arms.note: the operands after the opening group are skipped along with it, so `[a, b].map(function() {…})` is not acted on

arms.name: M-BOM-HAXE-SEAT
arms.note: the Haxe whole-file write drops the carry, so fmt and every canonicalising op strip a file byte-order mark

arms.name: M-HXSHAPE-JSONPRINTER-UNLISTED
arms.note: a direct JsonPrinter.print call no longer counts as rendering an object, so the fix changes what it prints

arms.name: M-HXSHAPE-COPY-UNLISTED
arms.note: a Reflect.copy no longer counts as enumerating an object, so the fix changes which fields the copy carries

arms.name: M-CHAIN-FITS-ONE-LINE
arms.find: { mode: WrapMode.NoWrap, conditions: [{ cond: WrapConditionType.ExceedsMaxLineLength, value: 0 }] },
arms.replace: { mode: WrapMode.OnePerLineAfterFirst, location: WrappingLocation.BeforeLast, conditions: [{ cond: WrapConditionType.ExceedsMaxLineLength, value: 0 }] },
arms.note: a chain that fits is laid one operator per line, so the default no longer keeps a fitting chain on one line

arms.name: M-CHAIN-BREAK-PACKS
arms.note: an overflowing chain packs its operands up to the limit and leaves the rest on a ragged last line instead of breaking at every operator

arms.name: M-TYPE-BODY-EDGE-NO-INTERFACE
arms.note: `interfaceEmptyLines.beginType` is parsed and dropped, so an interface body keeps the source edge

arms.name: M-FNBODY-COMMENT-EMPTY
arms.note: a body holding only a comment after its open brace counts as empty and its signature loses the additional indent

arms.name: M-LOADER-DEFAULT-INDENT-INHERIT
arms.note: a block restating defaultWrap inherits the built-in fallback indent of the mode it replaced

arms.name: M-LOADER-RULE-INDENT
arms.note: a configured rule additionalIndent is dropped at load time

arms.name: M-CHAIN-INDENT-UNREPORTED
arms.note: an indent stated on a chain cascade is accepted silently though the chain emitters never read it

arms.name: M-ANON-SEP-COND-NOT-SELF-ENDED
arms.note: a `#if … #end` field region owes a `,` after its `#end`, so an anon type with a guarded field followed by another field is refused

arms.name: M-ANON-SEP-FN-NOT-SELF-ENDED
arms.note: a `function` field is waived like a region, so `function f():Void {}` followed by another field parses though Haxe refuses a body there

arms.name: M-ANON-SEP-VAR-BRACE-NOT-SELF-ENDED
arms.note: a `var` field whose type ends with `}` owes a `,` before the next field, though Haxe's class notation takes the `}` for its `;`

arms.name: M-ANON-SEP-ARROW-NOT-BRACE-ENDED
arms.note: `var a:Int->{x:Int}` is not seen to end with `}`, so the next anon field is refused

arms.name: M-ANON-SEP-ARROW-FN-NOT-BRACE-ENDED
arms.note: `var a:(Int) -> {x:Int}` is not seen to end with `}`, so the next anon field is refused

arms.name: M-MACRO-PAREN-GLUED
arms.note: `macro` is written like the call-shaped `cast`, so `macro (x + 1)` loses the space the user keeps: it reads as a construct whose operand can be anything

arms.name: M-CAST-PAREN-SPACED
arms.note: `cast` is written like the construct `macro`, so `cast(x)` gains a space and stops reading as a call

arms.name: M-FNTYPE-NEST-TYPE-ARG-OFF
arms.note: a type argument is no longer marked nested, so a function type inside `Array<…>` or `Null<…>` loses the additional unit and continues one unit past its line

arms.name: M-FNTYPE-NEST-PARENS-OFF
arms.note: a parenthesised function type is no longer marked nested, so it continues one unit past its line instead of two

arms.name: M-FNTYPE-NEST-COND-OFF
arms.note: a function type inside a `#if` type arm is no longer marked nested, so it continues one unit past its line instead of two

arms.name: M-FNTYPE-NEST-NEW-OFF
arms.note: the type arguments of a `new` expression are no longer marked nested, so a function type among them continues one unit past its line instead of two

arms.name: M-FNTYPE-NEST-ABSTRACT-OFF
arms.note: an abstract's underlying type is no longer marked nested, so a function type there continues one unit past its line instead of two

arms.name: M-FNTYPE-NEST-ABSTRACT-HEAD-OFF
arms.note: an abstract head inside an #if arm no longer marks its underlying type nested, so a function type there continues one unit past its line instead of two

arms.name: M-EXTERN-CLASS-BETWEEN-DROPPED
arms.note: `externClassEmptyLines.betweenVars` is parsed and dropped, so an extern class stays tight between vars whatever the section says

arms.name: M-ENUM-ABSTRACT-BETWEEN-DROPPED
arms.note: `enumAbstractEmptyLines.betweenVars` is parsed and dropped, so an enum abstract keeps its default count

arms.name: M-ABSTRACT-BETWEEN-DROPPED
arms.note: `abstractEmptyLines.betweenVars` is parsed and dropped, so an abstract keeps its default count

arms.name: M-MACRO-CLASS-BETWEEN-DROPPED
arms.note: `macroClassEmptyLines.betweenVars` is parsed and dropped, so a macro class keeps its default count

arms.name: M-INTERFACE-EXISTING-DROPPED
arms.note: `interfaceEmptyLines.existingBetweenFields` is parsed and dropped, so an interface keeps its source blanks under `remove`

arms.name: M-MEMBER-GAP-POLICY-NO-SPLIT-LEAD
arms.note: the member-order policy stops reading the split lead, so it demands a before-doc blank above a split-led member that fmt never writes

arms.name: M-CASE-PATTERN-RULES-KEPT
arms.note: a `casePattern` block naming `defaultWrap` still runs the built-in rules, so that default and its location never answer

arms.name: M-CASE-PATTERN-IGNORE-CLEARS-RULES
arms.note: `ignore` drops the built-in rules, and the plain list then writes one flat line past the limit

arms.name: M-OBJLIT-GLUE-FORBODY-OFF
arms.note: the glue stops answering forBody: fitLine, so a comprehension literal goes back to Allman under it

arms.name: M-OBJLIT-GLUE-ABSENT-KEY
arms.note: an absent comprehensionFor stops deferring to forBody, though it means the same default

arms.name: M-OBJLIT-GLUE-EVERY-VALUE
arms.note: forBody overrides a comprehensionFor of keep or next, which place the body themselves

arms.name: M-LOADER-WRITES-THE-DEFAULT
arms.note: a config load re-baselines the shared default record

arms.name: M-ENUM-EXISTING-LEAKS
arms.note: enumEmptyLines.existingBetweenFields lands on the knob a class body reads, so an enum config rewrites class bodies

arms.name: M-ENUM-EXISTING-DROPPED
arms.note: enumEmptyLines.existingBetweenFields is parsed and dropped, so an enum body keeps its source blank lines

arms.name: M-CLASS-EXISTING-DROPPED
arms.note: classEmptyLines.existingBetweenFields is parsed and dropped, so a class body keeps its source blank lines

arms.name: M-ENUM-ABSTRACT-DOC-KEY-UNREAD
arms.note: `enumAbstractEmptyLines.beginTypeIfDocComments` is dropped on load, so an enum abstract holding a doc comment gets no blank after its `{`

arms.name: M-SAMELINE-KEEP-UNREPORTED
arms.note: a sameLine key stating keep loads as its default and no line says so

arms.name: M-KEEP-CLAUSE-SILENT
arms.note: the report finds the keep settings and prints nothing about them

arms.name: M-BODY-KEEP-NOT-DEFAULT
arms.note: an unsupported keep body policy overrides the knob instead of leaving its default

arms.name: M-TRAILING-COMMA-KEEP-MAPS-TO-REMOVE
arms.note: an explicit `keep` is read as `remove`, so the opt-out of the Remove default stops working

arms.name: M-TRAILING-COMMA-ABSENT-KEY-RESETS
arms.note: a wrapping section without the key resets the policy to Keep instead of leaving the default

arms.name: M-TRAILING-COMMA-ADD-KNOB-IMPLIES-REMOVE
arms.note: an add-knob config without wrapping.trailingComma loads as Remove, which silently voids the requested trailing comma

arms.name: M-METAVAR-REGIONS-OFF
arms.note: the lexer's regions are no longer consulted, so a metavariable inside a string, comment or regex literal of a pattern is rewritten to a placeholder

arms.name: M-DEFAULT-OBJECT-IGNORE
arms.note: the object-literal default stops being Ignore, so a short literal with a field block comment stays open around it

arms.name: M-DEFAULT-ARRAY-IGNORE
arms.note: the array and map default stops being Ignore, so a source break keeps a short list open

arms.name: M-DEFAULT-ANON-IGNORE
arms.note: the anonymous-type default stops being Ignore, so a short anon type with a field block comment stays open around it

arms.name: M-ANON-MULTILINE-ONE-PER-LINE
arms.note: the head rule of the anonymous-type cascade never fires, so an item a comment holds open is answered by a NoWrap rule

arms.name: M-HAXE-FACTS-FOR-FIX
arms.note: the Haxe grammar hands a fix no facts oracle, so every facts proof of a rule is silently off

arms.name: M-HAXE-FACTS-FIX-RUN
arms.note: the fix-run door offers no facts oracle although the run recorded its edits

arms.name: M-HAXE-FACTS-FOR-FILES
arms.note: the assisted phase is offered no facts oracle and goes to the display server

arms.name: M-TRY-OVERFLOW-KEY
arms.note: the key is ignored, so A cannot be selected

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-NAMES-READS-TEXT
arms.note: the names-first listing opens every module it names, so a module that cannot be read drops out of an answer a caller meant to get without any module text

arms.name: M-META-TYPE-UNWIRED
arms.note: a type declaration names no knob, so metadataType changes nothing

arms.name: M-META-ENUM-UNWIRED
arms.note: an enum constructor names no knob, so metadataOther does not reach it

arms.name: M-META-VARDECL-UNWIRED
arms.note: metadata after a var keyword answers the metadataOther knob again, so After breaks the declaration between the keyword and its name

arms.name: M-META-VARNAME-INLINE-SEP
arms.note: the binding name follows the source newline after the metadata run again

arms.name: M-META-MEMBER-VAR-ARM-OFF
arms.note: a var member has no arm of its own, so metadataVar stops reaching members and they take metadataOther

arms.name: M-META-MEMBER-FN-ARM-OFF
arms.note: a function member has no arm of its own, so metadataFunction stops reaching it

arms.name: M-META-ANON-VAR-ARM-OFF
arms.note: an anon var field takes metadataOther instead of metadataVar

arms.name: M-META-ANON-FN-ARM-OFF
arms.note: an anon function field takes metadataOther instead of metadataFunction

arms.name: M-META-ANON-OTHER-OFF
arms.note: an anon field without a keyword reaches no knob, so metadataOther does not move it

arms.name: M-META-CHAIN-UNWIRED
arms.note: a local var annotation is not a metadata site, so metadataVar does not reach it

arms.name: M-META-CONFIG-TYPE
arms.note: lineEnds.metadataType is read and dropped

arms.name: M-META-CONFIG-VAR
arms.note: lineEnds.metadataVar is read and dropped

arms.name: M-META-CONFIG-OTHER
arms.note: lineEnds.metadataOther is read and dropped

arms.name: M-META-DEFAULT-NONE
arms.note: a type's metadata defaults to None again, so it joins its declaration on one line

arms.name: M-META-TOP-VAR-ARM-OFF
arms.note: a module-level var answers to metadataType again, so metadataVar stops reaching it

arms.name: M-META-TOP-FN-ARM-OFF
arms.note: a module-level function answers to metadataType again, so metadataFunction stops reaching it

arms.name: M-ORACLE-HAXE-IS-SOURCE-ALWAYS
arms.note: every written file counts as a source the Haxe compiler parses, so a verification expects a parsed line for a file that can never have one

arms.name: M-ORACLE-HAXE-MODULE-UNDER-NULL
arms.note: no file is named by a module, so a module created by a write is never offered to a build and is judged unreached

arms.name: M-CONTAINER-ITEM-WRAP-CONFIG-IGNORED
arms.note: a configured containerItemWrap block is dropped and the built-in nested cascade stays, so a project cannot send simple literal arguments to their own line

arms.name: M-INTERSECTION-OPERAND-NOT-TYPEDEF-BODY
arms.note: an intersection operand of a typedef body is an ordinary anon type, so a Next left curly no longer lays it out one field per line

arms.name: M-ARROW-TYPE-IN-TYPEDEF-BODY
arms.note: an anon parameter or return of an old-style function type under a typedef counts as the typedef body, so a Next left curly lays it out one field per line

arms.name: M-ARROW-FN-TYPE-IN-TYPEDEF-BODY
arms.note: an anon parameter of a `(args) -> ret` function type under a typedef counts as the typedef body, so a Next left curly lays it out one field per line

arms.name: M-SEMI-ELSEIF-PER-LINE
arms.note: a value region's #elseif body takes one element per line, so it breaks between inline #if and #else branches

arms.name: M-COND-OPERAND-PAREN-GROUP
arms.note: a parenthesised condition is no operand, so the generated splice predicate stops before the infix operator after the group and the region skip-parses

arms.name: M-COND-GROUP-STOPS-AT-LINE
arms.note: a parenthesised group runs only to the end of its line, so `#if (` / `sys` / `)` on three lines is no condition

arms.name: M-COND-OPERATOR-OPERAND-SAME-LINE
arms.note: a `&&` after a flag and the flag after it, on this line or the next, join the condition, so `lime && x` reads as one condition instead of `lime` with the operator opening the body

arms.name: M-COND-NEGATION-OPERAND-SAME-LINE
arms.note: the operand of a `!` must sit on its line, so `!` / `sys` on two lines is no condition

arms.name: M-COND-GROUP-DEPTH-CAP
arms.note: a group nested inside a group is no piece of it, so the condition terminal rejects a nested `#if` group the way a depth-capped regex did

arms.name: M-COND-GROUP-QUOTE-BLIND
arms.note: a group's text runs over a quote, so a quoted `)` inside a group closes it, the condition terminal stops inside the string and the region no longer parses

arms.name: M-COND-GROUP-COMMENT-BLIND
arms.note: a block comment inside a group is read as condition text, so its quote opens a string or its paren closes the group and the region no longer parses

arms.name: M-COND-NUMBER-DOTTED
arms.note: a numeric operand stops at its dot, so `#if 4.2` reads `4` and leaves `.2` to the region body

arms.name: M-COND-QUOTED-OPERAND
arms.note: a quoted string is no condition operand, so a quoted `#if` condition carries no condition at all

arms.name: M-ENUM-CTOR-REGION-KW
arms.note: the enum body no longer recognises a `#if` region between its constructors, so a region of whole constructors stops parsing

arms.name: M-WHILE-COMPREHENSION-NOT-STRICT
arms.note: a while comprehension body is a plain fitLine body again, so a body that does not fit beside the head wraps the head's condition call instead of moving to the next line

arms.name: M-WHILE-COMPREHENSION-NO-BODY-POLICY
arms.note: a while comprehension body carries no body policy again, so comprehensionFor does not reach it: it glues to the head under next and stays at the head's indent when the source broke it

arms.name: M-ENUM-ABSTRACT-RULES-KEY-UNREAD
arms.note: `enumAbstractEmptyLines.abstractRulesUnlessValueList` is parsed and dropped, so every enum abstract body keeps the enumAbstract rules

arms.name: M-MEMBER-BEYOND-VALUE-NEVER
arms.note: no member counts as more than a value, so only a line comment hands a body to the abstract rules

arms.name: M-ABSTRACT-BODY-LINE-COMMENT-UNREAD
arms.note: a line comment above a value is no trigger, so line-comment groups close up under the key

arms.name: M-ABSTRACT-BODY-BEYOND-VALUES-ALWAYS
arms.note: every body counts as more than values, so a plain value list takes the abstract rules under the key

arms.name: M-MEMBER-PROPERTY-AS-VALUE
arms.note: a field with accessors counts as a value, so a property is no trigger

arms.name: M-MEMBER-STATIC-AS-VALUE
arms.note: a static member counts as a value, so a static var is no trigger

arms.name: M-MEMBER-METHOD-AS-VALUE
arms.note: a method counts as a value, so a function is no trigger

arms.name: M-COND-MEMBER-THEN-UNREAD
arms.note: a member in the then-branch of a `#if` region does not count, so the region reads as values

arms.name: M-COND-MEMBER-ELSEIF-UNREAD
arms.note: a member in an `#elseif` branch does not count

arms.name: M-COND-MEMBER-ELSE-UNREAD
arms.note: a member in the `#else` branch does not count

arms.name: M-COND-REGION-ALWAYS-BEYOND
arms.note: any `#if` region counts as beyond a value, so a region of plain values hands the body to the abstract rules

arms.name: M-ABSTRACT-BODY-TRAILING-COMMENT-READ
arms.note: a comment trailing a value counts as a group label, so a trailing line comment hands the body to the abstract rules

arms.name: M-MEMBER-FINAL-AS-BEYOND-VALUE
arms.replace: caseBindMulti(HX_CLASS_MEMBER, ['VarMember'], [0 => '_v'], macro _v.access != null), caseOf(HX_CLASS_MEMBER, ['FinalMember'], macro true)
arms.note: a final field counts as more than a value whatever its accessors, so a final value hands the body to the abstract rules

arms.name: M-INDENT-CHARACTER-UNREPORTED
arms.note: an indentation.character the loader cannot read keeps the default indent with nothing to say so

arms.name: M-VALUES-CLAUSE-SILENT
arms.note: the report finds the unreadable values and prints nothing about them

arms.name: M-ARROW-COLON-KEY-UNMAPPED
arms.note: whitespace.arrowParamColonPolicy is read and dropped, so the colon of a named function-type parameter stays tight under every value of the key

arms.name: M-CONSTRAINT-COLON-KEY-UNMAPPED
arms.note: whitespace.typeParamConstraintColonPolicy is read and dropped, so the colon of a type-parameter constraint stays tight under every value of the key

arms.name: M-ARROW-COLON-ABSENT-TIGHT
arms.note: an absent whitespace.arrowParamColonPolicy keeps the function-type parameter colon tight instead of following typeHintColonPolicy

arms.name: M-CONSTRAINT-COLON-ABSENT-TIGHT
arms.note: an absent whitespace.typeParamConstraintColonPolicy keeps the type-parameter constraint colon tight instead of following typeHintColonPolicy

arms.name: M-META-FIT-ARGS-IGNORED
arms.note: every metadata call reads as simple, so a call or several arguments no longer break the run

arms.name: M-META-FIT-INTERP-PLAIN
arms.note: an interpolated string argument reads as simple

arms.name: M-META-FIT-MULTILINE-PLAIN
arms.note: a string argument spanning lines reads as simple

arms.name: M-META-FIT-PATH-OFF
arms.note: a dotted-path argument reads as complex

arms.name: M-META-FIT-LITERAL-OFF
arms.note: a number or bool argument reads as complex

arms.name: M-META-FIT-UNMAPPED
arms.note: lineEnds value fit falls to none

arms.name: M-META-FIT-TYPE-UNWIRED
arms.note: module-level metadata names no simplicity predicate, so fit breaks it one per line

arms.name: M-META-FIT-MEMBER-UNWIRED
arms.note: member metadata names no simplicity predicate, so fit breaks it one per line

arms.name: M-META-FIT-ENUM-UNWIRED
arms.note: enum constructor metadata names no simplicity predicate, so fit breaks it one per line

arms.name: M-META-FIT-ANON-UNWIRED
arms.note: anon field metadata names no simplicity predicate, so fit breaks it one per line

arms.name: M-META-FIT-CHAIN-UNWIRED
arms.note: a local var's metadata names no simplicity predicate, so fit breaks it

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-BASELINE
arms.note: the edit is written over the compiled defaults instead of the baseline the call started from, so an empty document assigns the six body policies and the curly blanks the loader re-baselines

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-LITERAL-ONLY
arms.note: every argument reads as an empty document, so a variable or a concatenation is rewritten as if it were a literal instead of refused

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-IGNORED-KEY
arms.note: a document setting a key the loader does not act on is rewritten as if every key were read, so the typed edit silently drops it

arms.name: M-PATTERN-SEQ-FIRST-ONLY
arms.note: a multi-statement pattern keeps only its first statement, so the rest is silently dropped and the search is wider than written

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-STRICTJSON-SITE
arms.note: the kit's own strictJson call is not a call shape, so it is left as the JSON it loads instead of becoming the typed edit

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-FIXTURE-SITE
arms.note: a HxWriteFixture.triviaWrite call is not a call shape, so its JSON configuration argument stays a string

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-ARGUMENT-ONLY
arms.note: a fixture call is replaced whole by the typed edit, so the source text it was given is dropped along with the configuration

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-ALREADY-TYPED
arms.note: a fixture call whose configuration is already the typed edit is refused as a non-literal argument, so a second run over a migrated file fails

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-NESTED-FIXTURE
arms.find: final refusal: Null<String> = nestedEdits(source, run, edits);
arms.note: a fixture call inside another fixture call's source argument is not read, so the outer call is migrated and the inner one keeps its JSON

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-NAMED-FINAL
arms.note: no final is read as a named configuration, so an argument naming a constant final is refused as a non-literal argument

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-CONCATENATION
arms.note: a concatenation of string literals is no constant string, so it is refused instead of read as one document

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-INLINE-CUT
arms.note: a retyped inline final keeps its inline modifier, so its initializer, now a call, does not compile

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-PUBLIC-FINAL
arms.note: a public final is retyped though another module may read it as a string

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-NAMED-READERS
arms.note: a final read outside a configuration call is retyped anyway, so that reader is left expecting the string

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-FIELD-READ
arms.note: a final read as a field is retyped anyway, a read the binding walk does not see

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-TYPED-VALUE
arms.note: a fixture call reading a value typed as the options is refused as a non-literal argument, so a second run over a retyped final fails

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-FINAL-CLASS
arms.note: a member final of a class a subclass in another module may extend is retyped, so that subclass reading it as a string no longer compiles

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-GUARDED-PUBLIC
arms.note: a final public only under a conditional region is retyped, so another module reading it under that define no longer compiles

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-GUARDED-INLINE
arms.note: a final inline only under a conditional region is retyped, keeping an inline over a call initializer that does not compile under that define

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-ACCESS-GRANT
arms.note: a member final opened to another module by an access-granting meta, on it or on its type, is retyped though that module may read it as a string

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-NO-SUBJECT
arms.note: no call is a loader subject, so a test whose options are only read by field is rewritten into a tautology

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-ASSERT-SUBJECT
arms.note: a field read under an assertion is no subject unless every read is by field, so a test that also hands its options to a writer is rewritten into a tautology

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-EMPTY-FORK
arms.note: a {} document becomes forkWith(edited -> {}) instead of the bare baseline

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-LISTS-KEEP-SOURCE
arms.note: a listsKeepSource call is no wrapper, so its argument is read as the document and the call is refused as no constant string

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-LISTS-KEEP-SOURCE-NAMED
arms.note: a final read under the wrapper is retyped without what the wrapper adds

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-LISTS-KEEP-SOURCE-MIXED
arms.note: a final read both under the wrapper and outside it is retyped anyway, so one of its readers gets the wrong document

arms.name: M-TYPED-OPTIONS-LISTS-KEEP-SOURCE-OWN
arms.note: a test's own listsKeepSource helper is read as the fixture's wrapper, so its document is rewritten with list wraps it never had

arms.name: M-LISTS-KEEP-SOURCE-KEEP-ANON
arms.note: the typed counterpart leaves the anonymous-type wrap on its default fallback, so it no longer loads like the wrapped document

arms.name: M-COND-SIBLINGS-KEY-IGNORED
arms.note: sameLine.conditionalSiblings is read and dropped, so a config that asked for off still shares the branches of a region

arms.name: M-UNTYPED-KW-COMMENT-DROPPED
arms.note: `untyped` grows no kw-trivia args, so the comment between `untyped` and its operand is dropped at parse

arms.name: M-TYPEPARAM-META-UNDECLARED
arms.note: a type parameter declares no metadata run, so `<@:const N>` and `<T:Foo = Bar, @:const N>` stop parsing

arms.name: M-TYPEPARAM-CONSTRAINT-AFTER-LEAD-OFF
arms.note: the constraint has no AfterLead slot, so a comment after its colon is dropped and the writer round trip refuses the file

arms.name: M-TYPEPARAM-DEFAULT-AFTER-LEAD-OFF
arms.note: the default has no AfterLead slot, so a comment after its `=` is dropped and the writer round trip refuses the file

arms.name: M-COND-QUOTED-ESCAPE-OFF
arms.note: a backslash no longer hides the character after it, so an escaped quote ends a condition literal early

arms.name: M-COND-QUOTED-UNTERMINATED
arms.note: a literal with no closing quote is read as closed, so the rest of an unterminated condition is read as a value

arms.name: M-COND-FLAG-DOTTED
arms.note: a flag stops at its first dot, so `a.b` reads `a` and leaves `.b` as trailing text

arms.name: M-CONDVALUE-AND-LOOSE
arms.note: `&&` binds like `||`, so `a || b && c` groups left to right

arms.name: M-CONDVALUE-CMP-LOOSE
arms.note: `==` binds looser than `||`, so `a == b || c` compares `a` with the whole disjunction

arms.name: M-CONDVALUE-CMP-RIGHT
arms.note: `==` groups to the right, so a chain of comparisons nests the other way

arms.name: M-CONDVALUE-NOT-GONE
arms.note: `!` is no prefix operator of a condition

arms.name: M-CONDVALUE-GTEQ-SHADOWED
arms.note: `>=` is never matched, so `a >= b` reads `a > ` and fails on the `=`

arms.name: M-CONDVALUE-VERSION-FLAG
arms.note: `version(` is not a call of its own, so it reads as the flag `version` followed by trailing text

arms.name: M-CONDVALUE-GROUP-BRACKET
arms.note: a group is written in brackets, so a parenthesised condition is no operand

arms.name: M-COND-VALUE-SCHEMA-LINE-COMMENT
arms.note: a condition is read with the Haxe whitespace, so a `//` comment is a blank where the compiler refuses it
